# Telegram Automation GUI

> A desktop GUI for Telegram user-account automation, available as a standalone Windows EXE and Python source, built with Telethon and Tkinter. English and Chinese interfaces. 中文：Telegram 个人号定时签到、群聊消息和可选 AI 回复工具。

The UI has Connection, Tasks, AI connection, and Activity pages. Each task has its own searchable group selector. Tasks include daily check-ins, scheduled messages from a fixed pool or an AI provider, and optional AI replies. Login uses Telegram application credentials, a phone number, a verification code, and a two-step verification password when required; this is a personal-account client, not a Bot API bot.

Windows 64-bit users can [download the standalone EXE](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/releases/latest/download/TelegramAutomation-Windows-x64.exe) and double-click it without installing Python or Git. Executables are published in GitHub Releases, while the repository contains source code. Settings and Telegram sessions are saved automatically beside the EXE. To update, fully quit, replace the EXE, and keep the configuration and session files. Developers can run the source with `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` and `python main.py`, which requires Python with Tkinter. Fresh configurations disable all tasks and the proxy, and start with an empty message pool. Start with one permitted check-in group and leave other tasks disabled. Save settings persists the configuration without starting tasks. Save & start validates, saves, and starts enabled tasks. Check-ins use the computer's local time with an additional random 0–5 minute delay. Scheduled-message active hours support crossing midnight.

The language selector saves its choice and preserves custom text and pending edits. Built-in AI prompts request English for the English interface and Chinese for the Chinese interface; empty prompts use the selected language's default, while custom prompts remain unchanged. New configurations follow the system language; existing configurations without a language field retain Chinese. The background-operation preference is saved, and the Activity view bounds retained log history.

On Windows, fonts and layout follow the system's display scaling for high DPI/4K displays. Fully quit and reopen the app after updating; no manual configuration or Windows display-scaling changes are needed.

AI tasks share an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint and require a provider key. AI replies send up to 10 recent messages; scheduled AI messages use up to 12, including sender names. Test current connection uses the current AI fields without saving them, includes no group history, and does not change Telegram login state. Test requests may incur provider charges. Local config/session files contain sensitive credentials without application-level encryption. Use only where group rules permit automation. No LICENSE file is currently provided; reuse permission should be confirmed with the maintainer.

## Documentation

- [Windows EXE download](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/releases/latest/download/TelegramAutomation-Windows-x64.exe): Standalone 64-bit Windows application; no separate Python or Git installation.
- [Releases](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/releases): Executable downloads and release notes.
- [English guide](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/README.md): Setup, tasks, language selection, saving, troubleshooting, and data handling.
- [中文说明](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/README.zh-CN.md): Chinese guide to the same workflows.
- [First-run walkthrough](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/README.md#first-run): Connect a personal account and configure one daily check-in task.
- [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/README.md#troubleshooting): Tkinter, proxy, task, language, schedule, and AI connection checks.
- [Report a problem](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/issues/new?template=bug_report.md): Include app version, environment, and interface-language details with a redacted error excerpt.
- [Configuration example](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/config.example.json): Review proxy, task, and provider settings before using the example.
- [Dependencies](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/requirements.txt): Python packages required to run the application.

## Source

- [Application entry point](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/main.py): Starts the UI, configures logging, and handles startup errors.
- [Desktop interface](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/ui.py): Tkinter pages, language switching, login, task configuration, activity, and tray integration.
- [DPI support](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/dpi.py): Windows DPI awareness and monitor metrics.
- [Display scaling](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/display.py): Scales fonts and layout dimensions with the display DPI.
- [Automation engine](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/engine.py): Telethon authentication, scheduling, group messages, and AI requests.
- [Configuration defaults](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/config.py): Runtime defaults, bilingual prompts, legacy migration, and local configuration persistence.
- [Settings validation](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/validation.py): Checks connection settings and enabled workflows.
- [UI translations](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/ui_i18n.py): English and Chinese interface labels.
- [Engine translations](https://github.com/Marco0431/telegram-automation-gui/blob/main/engine_i18n.py): English and Chinese activity messages.
